record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Classify all ε-hermitian variation structures for G=Z, writing a structure as (U;b,h,V) with h=ρ(1) and V=V(1), beyond the already classified simple structures. The classification should include degenerate and non-simple cases such as indecomposable variation structures whose monodromy h has more than one Jordan block, identify natural restrictions that occur for simple structures V(f) coming from isolated hypersurface singularities, and classify the structures satisfying those restrictions, including a class containing the structures produced by hypersurface singularities with one-dimensional singular locus.

evidence.quote: They deﬁne an indecomposable (+1)-HVS, but the automorphism h has two Jordan blocks. Note that even the associated (degenerate) isometric structure (b, h) is indecomposable.
In this section G = Z and the system V = (U ; b, h, V ) denotes h = ρ(1) and V = V (1).

Problem # 3. Classify the variation structures for G = Z (cf. Example 11). Any hypersurface isolated singularity gives a simple variation structure (of G = Z) (cf. Example 4). Find natural restrictions provided by the singularity theory, and classify variation structures with the corresponding restrictions. Classify a class of variation structures which includes the structures given by hypersurface singularities with one–dimensional singular locus.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix ε ∈ {+1,−1} and let G = Z. An ε-hermitian variation structure (HVS) over Z is a quadruple V = (U; b, h, V) where:
- U is a finite-dimensional complex vector space;
- b : U × U → C is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian form (i.e. b(y,x) = ε·conj(b(x,y))), allowed to be degenerate in the generalized sense considered below;
- h : U → U is a b-isometric automorphism (the monodromy), so b(h x, h y) = b(x,y);
- V : U → U is a C-linear endomorphism (the variation operator) satisfying the compatibility b(V x, y) + ε·conj(b(x, V y)) + b(V x, V y) = ... encoded by the standard relation V = h − I composed with the duality induced by b on the non-degenerate part, in such a way that V determines (and is determined by) h on the non-degenerate part of U.
Two such structures are isomorphic via b-isometries that intertwine h and V. The structure is called simple when b is non-degenerate; otherwise it is degenerate. It is indecomposable if it is not isomorphic to an orthogonal direct sum of two non-trivial ε-HVS.

The simple ε-hermitian variation structures over Z (equivalently, with monodromy h whose every generalized eigenspace forms a single Jordan block of fixed size) have a known complete classification into indecomposable building blocks.

Problem. Classify all ε-hermitian variation structures (U; b, h, V) for G = Z beyond the simple case. In particular:

(a) Classify the indecomposable ε-HVS whose monodromy h has more than one Jordan block (so that even the associated isometric structure (b, h), which may be degenerate, is indecomposable).

(b) Identify the natural restrictions on (U; b, h, V) that are forced when V = V(f) arises from the Milnor fibration / variation operator of an isolated hypersurface singularity f : (C^{n+1}, 0) → (C, 0), and classify all ε-HVS satisfying these restrictions.

(c) Classify a class of ε-HVS large enough to include every variation structure produced by a germ of a hypersurface singularity with one-dimensional singular locus.
artifact.category_tag: Hermitian variation structures of hypersurface singularities
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaces follow-up work on Hermitian variation structures, real Seifert forms, Blanchfield pairings and Hodge-type link invariants that extend the classification of simple ε-HVS, but no source clearly states a full classification of degenerate/non-simple indecomposable variation structures over G = Z, of the restrictions imposed by isolated hypersurface singularities, or of the class covering hypersurface singularities with one-dimensional singular locus. The status of the problem as a whole appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Real Seifert forms, Hodge numbers and Blanchfield pairings
status_evidence.snippet: Develops and refines the theory of Hermitian variation structures, extending the simple-case classification but not asserting a full classification of the degenerate and non-simple cases.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work refines but does not fully classify non-simple ε-HVS over Z.

status_evidence.title: Hodge–type structures as link invariants
status_evidence.snippet: Uses HVS as link invariants of singularities; treats restrictions coming from singularity theory but in restricted settings.
status_evidence.claim: Singularity-theoretic restrictions on HVS are studied but a full classification including one-dimensional singular locus is not stated.
